title: Implement Array.prototype.myReduce (Compliant Spec)
subtopicTitle: Core Array & Utility Polyfills from Scratch
problemStatement: Implement `myReduce(callback, initialValue)` on `Array.prototype`. If `initialValue` is not provided, the first non-empty element is used as the accumulator and iteration begins at the next non-empty index. Throws `TypeError` if invoked on an empty array without an initialValue.
interviewTrap: Checking `if (!initialValue)` breaks when `initialValue` is `0`, `false`, or `''`! You MUST check `arguments.length > 1`.

testCases.name: Throws TypeError on empty array with no initialValue
testCases.testFn: try { [].myReduce((a, b) => a + b); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; }

details.name: Throws TypeError on empty array with no initialValue

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Native array methods must respect sparse arrays (`in` operator check), handle absent `initialValue` in `reduce` (skipping holes to find the first real element), and preserve the caller's prototype chain.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Accumulator State & Initial Value Resolution.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Accumulator State & Initial Value Resolution is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Checking `if (!initialValue)` breaks when `initialValue` is `0`, `false`, or `''`! You MUST check `arguments.length > 1`.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What happens if reduce() is called on an empty array without an initialValue?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Per ECMA-262 §23.1.3.24, calling `reduce` on an empty array without an `initialValue` MUST throw a `TypeError: Reduce of empty array with no initial value`.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: If no initialValue is provided, what is used as the initial accumulator?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: The first non-empty element in the array is used as the initial accumulator, and iteration begins at the NEXT index (index 1 if index 0 was populated).

realWorldUseCases.description: Reducing a flat list of transactions into category totals.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const totals = txs.reduce((acc, t) => { acc[t.cat] = (acc[t.cat] || 0) + t.amount; return acc; }, {});

howToExplain.opening: Array.prototype.reduce accumulates elements into a single value, requiring careful handling of initial accumulator resolution and empty array validation.
keyPoints: Throws TypeError if array is empty and no initialValue is supplied.
If initialValue is omitted, the first non-empty element becomes accumulator.
Skips sparse array holes during iteration.
Capable of implementing map, filter, and flat through reduction.
howToExplain.closingImpression: reduce is the universal catamorphism of arrays: almost all other array methods can be expressed as a reduction.
analogies: A snowball rolling down a hill: it starts with an initial core (initialValue) and picks up snow with every turn until it reaches the bottom.

commonMistakes.mistake: Defaulting initialValue to 0 or null when omitted.
commonMistakes.why: When initialValue is omitted, the FIRST array element must be used as the accumulator.
commonMistakes.correct: Track whether an initial value was provided by checking arguments.length > 1.

followUpDeepDive.question: Why is Array.prototype.reduceRight needed?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `reduceRight` iterates in reverse (from length-1 down to 0). It is essential for function composition pipelines (`compose`) where functions evaluate right-to-left.
